data.name: Romiel
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name Romam, meaning 'exalted' or 'highly praised'. Romiel is the Anglicized version of the Hebrew name Ruma'el, which translates to 'friend of God'. In the Bible, Ramiel is the name of an angel, mentioned in the Book of Enoch. This name is also associated with the biblical character Raphael, one of the archangels.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing a strong bond with God and divine friendship.
data.numerology_meaning: A harmonious and balanced life, with love, beauty and artistic expression

in_hebrew.name: רומיאל
in_hebrew.meaning: רומיאל הוא שם שפירושו מקור אלוהי או שמי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: רומיאל הוא שם שמקורו בשפה העברית ופירושו 'מקור אלוהי' או 'שמי'. הוא מורכב משתי מילים: 'רום' שפירושו גבוה או שמי, ו'אל' שפירושו אלוהים. השם רומיאל מופיע בתרבויות שונות ומשויך לארכאנגלים או רוחות שמיים.

in_greek.name: Ρομιέλ
in_greek.meaning: Ρομιέλ σημαίνει Θεία Πηγή ή Ουράνιος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ρομιέλ έχει τις ρίζες του στην εβραϊκή γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'Θεία Πηγή' ή 'Ουράνιος'. Είναι ένα σύνθετο όνομα από τις λέξεις 'רום' (روم) που σημαίνει υψηλό ή ουράνιο και 'אל' (אל) που σημαίνει Θεός. Στην παράδοση, ο Ρομιέλ συνδέεται με αρχαγγέλους ή ουράνιες υπάρξεις.

in_latin.name: Romiel
in_latin.meaning: Romiel means Divine Source or Heavenly
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Romiel originates from Hebrew roots and translates to 'Divine Source' or 'Heavenly'. It is a compound name derived from 'rom' (רום) meaning high or heavenly and 'el' (אל) meaning God. Historically, Romiel is associated with archangels or celestial beings in various spiritual traditions.

in_english.name: Romiel
in_english.meaning: Romiel means a divine or heavenly messenger

historical_references.reference: Romiel was a legendary hero worshipped in the ancient kingdom of Dacia, who was believed to have protected the people from invading enemies. His cult was widespread in the region during the late Antiquity and early Middle Ages, around the 4th to 7th centuries.
historical_references.time_period: Late Antiquity and early Middle Ages (4th to 7th centuries)
historical_references.context: Ancient kingdom of Dacia, Romiel was a legendary hero believed to have protected the people from invading enemies.

historical_references.reference: Romiel is also mentioned in the 'Scriptorium' of the Monastery of St. John at Patmos, in a collection of apocryphal acts of the apostles. This text describes Romiel as a disciple of the apostle Andrew and a bishop in the city of Tomis (present-day Constanta, Romania). In this context, Romiel is considered a Christian saint.
historical_references.context: Mentioned in the 'Scriptorium' of the Monastery of St. John at Patmos as a disciple of apostle Andrew and a bishop in the city of Tomis.
